newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: U.S. envoy sees limitless growth for Africa.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy sees limitless growth for Africa.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton's envoy to a four-day African-American summit pledged on Friday to convince U.S. businesses of Africa's potential as a trading partner.

Transportation Secretary Ronald Slater said his department was already working with commercial officials in U.S. embassies across Africa to identify transport opportunities, and added he would encourage private companies to develop Africa.
"My objective is to persuade them to invest in Africa. The potential of the sub-Saharan market is immense. I plan to return as soon as possible," he told Reuters.

In an address to the summit, at which a host of African leaders have tried to drum up investment from U.S. companies, Slater said his government was committed to a burgeoning involvement in the world's poorest continent.
"I plan to work closely with U.S. transportation companies, helping them to learn more about Africa's emerging markets and encouraging them to be active players in developing those markets," he said.
"The U.S. government and private sector want to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with sub-Saharan Africa as they become full partners in the global economy."

Slater cautioned African leaders however that the U.S. government expected them to push ahead with political and economic reform to unlock the promised $650 million in funds set aside for infrastructural and equity investments.

He also urged East Africa to form a regional trade bloc and for southern and West Africa to consolidate their regional efforts, adding: "A united Africa is far stronger than a divided Africa. There will be growing pains but of this comes a new promise."
Slater did not elaborate on any specific projects he wanted to undertake in Africa, saying he would seek to finalise these on his next trip ahead of a planned visit by President Clinton.
The African/African American summit closes in the Zimbabwean capital later on Friday.
